strengths: The proposed method, Causal2Vec, addresses the inherent limitations of causal attention in decoder-only LLMs without requiring architectural modifications or sequence-lengthening tricks like text repetition.

The approach is computationally highly efficient, requiring up to 85% shorter sequence lengths and up to 82% lower inference time compared to competitive causal-attention baselines like ECHO and bge-en-icl.

The paper provides a comprehensive evaluation on the full Massive Text Embeddings Benchmark (MTEB) across multiple model sizes (1.3B to 7B parameters), demonstrating state-of-the-art results among models trained on the same public retrieval dataset.
The ablation studies are thorough, investigating critical hyperparameters and design choices such as the number of contextual tokens, their position, and whether to freeze the bidirectional encoder.
weaknesses: The method introduces a hybrid dependency by requiring an external bidirectional encoder (E5-base-v2). While lightweight (110M parameters), this slightly complicates the deployment pipeline compared to a pure single-model LLM setup.

The gains from the specific token concatenation strategy (Contextual + EOS) are somewhat marginal on larger models (e.g., Mistral-7B improves from 67.60 to 67.79 on MTEB-MINI compared to using just the last-token pooling with the contextual token).

The comparison is strictly limited to models trained on public retrieval data. While this ensures a fair comparison, it remains unclear how well Causal2Vec scales when trained on the massive, diverse, and synthetic mixtures used by top-tier MTEB leaders.

strengths: Well-motivated approach that addresses the limitations of causal attention in decoder-only LLM embedding models without modifying the core model architecture or attention masks.

Outstanding balance of performance and efficiency: achieves state-of-the-art or highly competitive performance on the MTEB benchmark while reducing the required sequence length by up to 85% and inference time by up to 82% compared to leading causal-based methods like ECHO and bge-en-icl.

Comprehensive and thorough ablation studies that explore key hyperparameters and design choices, such as the number and position of Contextual tokens, freezing vs. fine-tuning the bidirectional encoder, and different bidirectional encoder backbones.
weaknesses: Dependency on an external bidirectional encoder (e.g., E5-base-v2). While lightweight (110M parameters), it adds architectural complexity, requiring a two-stage forward pass and dual-model management.

The final embedding is obtained by concatenating the representation of the Contextual token and the EOS token, which doubles the embedding dimension (from $d$ to $2d$). The paper should discuss the implications of this increased dimensionality on downstream vector database storage and retrieval latency.

strengths: An elegant and simple approach to bypass the causal attention limitation of decoder-only LLMs without modifying their core attention mechanism or codebase, preserving the pre-trained weights' integrity.
Significant reduction in sequence length (up to 85%) and inference time (up to 82%) compared to existing causal-preserving methods like ECHO or bge-en-icl, making it highly efficient.
Thorough evaluation across multiple LLM backbones (1.3B to 7B) on the full MTEB benchmark (56 datasets), demonstrating consistent improvements over baseline LLMs.

Extensive ablation studies that systematically investigate different configurations, including the position of the contextual token, the number of tokens, and the choice of freezing vs. tuning the bidirectional encoder.
weaknesses: A major conceptual limitation lies in the representation method. In the sequence [I; C; T; EOS], the Contextual token C cannot attend to the subsequent text tokens T or EOS due to the causal attention mask of the LLM. Therefore, the last hidden state of C at the output layer of the LLM does not contain any contextual information processed by the LLM itself regarding T; it only contains the initial representation from the bidirectional encoder. The paper should explicitly discuss this unidirectional bottleneck of the LLM's processing on the Contextual token.

High parameter and computational overhead for marginal gains. The method requires running a bidirectional encoder (e.g., E5-base-v2, 110M params) in addition to the decoder LLM (e.g., Mistral-7B). Given that E5-base-v2 alone is already a strong text embedder, adding a 7B parameter LLM for a relatively small performance boost raises questions about practical utility in real-world resource-constrained scenarios.

The comparison is restricted only to models trained on public retrieval datasets. While this ensures a fair comparison under controlled data setups, it limits the understanding of how Causal2Vec positions itself against actual state-of-the-art general-purpose embedders that leverage broader synthetic or multi-task datasets.

strengths: Clear motivation addressing the trade-offs of existing decoder-only embedding models (attention mismatch in bidirectional models vs. high computational cost in input-duplication or prompting methods).

Simple and effective design: prepending a single Contextual token distilled from a lightweight bidirectional encoder elegantly bypasses the causal bottleneck without altering the attention mechanism of the LLM.
Comprehensive evaluation across multiple LLM backbones (from 1.3B to 7B parameters) on the full MTEB benchmark, achieving state-of-the-art results among models trained on public retrieval datasets.
Thorough ablation studies analyzing alternative pooling strategies, different bidirectional encoders, number of contextual tokens, and robustness to noise.
weaknesses: Doubled embedding dimension: Concatenating the Contextual and EOS tokens doubles the final embedding dimension (e.g., to 8192 for 7B models), which increases downstream storage, indexing, and search costs in vector databases.
System complexity: The method introduces dependency on an external bidirectional encoder, adding some complexity to the overall model pipeline during both training and deployment.
Evaluation is limited to English datasets, leaving the performance and generalizability of Causal2Vec in multilingual retrieval scenarios unexplored.

strengths: The proposed method, Causal2Vec, addresses the representational limitations of causal attention in decoder-only LLMs without converting to bidirectional attention, avoiding the pre-train/fine-tune mismatch issue.

Highly efficient compared to recent sequence-expansion approaches like ECHO (which repeats the input) or bge-en-icl (which prepends multiple in-context examples). It only adds a single contextual token, maintaining standard sequence lengths.

Comprehensive evaluation across four LLM backbones (ranging from 1.3B to 7B) on the full MTEB benchmark (56 datasets), demonstrating clear improvements and achieving state-of-the-art results among academically comparable models.
Extensive and rigorous ablation studies that validate the choice of contextual token position, count, pooling/representation strategies, and robustness to noise.
weaknesses: The method introduces a heterogeneous inference pipeline, requiring a separate bidirectional encoder (e.g., E5-base) to be run prior to the decoder LLM, which adds system deployment complexity compared to pure single-model architectures.

Concatenating the Contextual and EOS tokens doubles the final embedding dimension (e.g., to 8192 for Mistral-7B), which increases storage overhead and indexing costs in downstream vector search databases.

strengths: Presents a simple and intuitive solution (Causal2Vec) to overcome the representation limitations of causal attention in decoder-only LLMs without modifying their core architectures.

Achieves impressive empirical performance on the comprehensive MTEB benchmark, outperforming several state-of-the-art bidirectional and causal LLM embedding methods across multiple model scales (1.3B to 7B parameters).
Provides substantial efficiency gains in terms of both inference latency and sequence length compared to existing causal methods like ECHO and bge-en-icl.
Includes thorough and detailed ablation studies exploring the position of the token, number of contextual tokens, impact of freezing/unfreezing the bi-encoder, and robustness to noise.
weaknesses: The approach is hybrid in nature, relying heavily on a separate, pre-trained bidirectional encoder (like E5). This undermines the goal of utilizing a pure decoder-only LLM, introducing pipeline complexity and dependency on external embedders.

Concatenating the Contextual and EOS tokens doubles the final output embedding dimension (e.g., up to 8192 dimensions for 7B models). This significantly increases downstream storage requirements, indexing time, and retrieval latency in vector databases, which limits its real-world applicability.

The conceptual critique of bidirectional attention causing 'pre-train/fine-tune mismatch' is somewhat undermined by the proposed solution, which itself prepends a projected, out-of-distribution contextual token directly into the sequence, introducing its own form of representation mismatch.
